summary: Safe demote and fallback plan for tenant optimizer tuning after throughput regression
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a sudden ~25-40% drop in throughput and elevated tail latency after pushing an optimizer 'demotion' profile and turning on aggressive per-tenant KV-prefetch+quant settings. Impact: Several production routes for BrightHealth AI seeing request queuing and occasional 504s during peak window (09:00-11:30 PST). Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated-35), prod-us-west with regional fallback to us-east. Affected models: redwood-gpt-medium-v2 (primary), open-gptj-6b (fallback variant). Steps to reproduce: 1) Use tenant config 'brighthealth/optimizer/profile-2026-03-09' on dedicated-35. 2) Send steady traffic (RPS ~120) with median seq length 512 and burst spikes to 900 RPS. 3) Observe autoscaler behavior and request queue on serving nodes. Observed behavior: After profile activation, per-GPU throughput falls, KV cache eviction increases, and prefetch tasks saturate background I/O; the runtime starts queuing requests and occasionally returns 504 gateway timeouts. Expected behavior: Slight improvement in token cost and similar or better throughput; no increased 504s. Initial hypothesis: The demotion profile increased background prefetch concurrency and lowered per-request batching windows, causing more KV churn and I/O contention. Another contributor may be an interaction between quantization path and the chosen kernel selection for long sequences. Current mitigation attempts already taken: - Rolled traffic partially to fallback model 'open-gptj-6b' via console route split (50/50) — reduced errors but throughput still degraded. - Temp reduced prefetch concurrency to 2 via a feature flag for tenant, partial improvement. - Increased node pool by 2 GPUs; autoscaler lag observed. Ask/request from customer: Help craft a safe rollback/demotion-offramp that can be applied per-tenant without needing cluster-wide redeploy; recommend minimal-impact steps and console actions, and confirm whether model pinning to a previous kernel/quantization profile is necessary. Also request postmortem checklist items and a suggested conservative config for re-testing.
steps_to_reproduce: Activate tenant optimizer profile brighthealth/optimizer/profile-2026-03-09 on dedicated-35
Generate steady traffic at ~120 RPS with bursts to 900 RPS (median seq length 512)
Watch serving pod metrics: request_queue_depth, kv_cache_evictions, prefetch_task_queue, gpu_utilization
Observe increased 504s and long tail latencies after ~10-20 minutes
investigation_notes: 03-10T16:00: Support captured tenant config diff against baseline; prefetch_concurrency increased from 2->8, batch_window_ms reduced 40->10
03-10T17:14: Engineering hypothesis: high prefetch concurrency combined with shorter batch window produced smaller batches and higher per-token overhead on sequence lengths >256
03-10T18:01: Trace shows increased KVS reads/writes and an elevated rate of page faults on one node (node-awa-7); logs indicate repeated kernel-selection fallback for quantized path
03-11T09:22: SRE reproduced reduction in throughput in staging by applying same profile against redwood-gpt-medium-v2 with synthetic load; confirmed higher IO and smaller average batch sizes
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Opening ticket after customer reported production impact at 09:30 PST. Collecting logs and config diffs.
BrightHealth Ops (customer) 2026-03-10: We need a safe way to step back that doesn't require full pool redeploy — we prefer per-tenant rollback and routing guidance.
Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-10: Requesting stack traces and node-level iostat output for node-awa-7. Starting staging repro run.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-11: Staging confirms regression. Proposed temporary mitigations: 1) Reduce prefetch_concurrency to 1; 2) Increase batch_window_ms to 60 for tenant; 3) Create a per-tenant traffic-split to fallback model and monitor 95/99p latency for 30m.
BrightHealth Ops (customer) 2026-03-11: Applied suggested mitigations; 504s reduced pero still seeing 20% lower throughput than baseline. Asking about snapshot restore option.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-12: We can restore tenant config snapshot 'brighthealth/snap-2026-03-08' via console; this is non-disruptive and can be gated per-route. Planning to apply at 14:00 PST after validation window.
resolution: Workaround applied: restored tenant config to snapshot brighthealth/snap-2026-03-08 and applied a conservative per-tenant demotion policy: prefetch_concurrency=1, batch_window_ms=60, kv_prefetch_enabled=false. Also implemented a temporary traffic split 80% -> redwood-gpt-medium-v2 (pinned to kernel v1.12) / 20% -> open-gptj-6b for safety. Outcome: 504s returned to baseline and throughput recovered to ~95% of original within 45 minutes. Follow-up items: engineering to add an automated 'tenant-snapshot-restore' console button (ENG-ops ticket created), add a warning in optimizer UI when prefetch_concurrency>4 for long-sequence tenants, and schedule a deeper kernel/quant interaction investigation (linked PR created).
